8:17.sourceText: ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο, σπουδαιότερος δὲ ὑπάρχων αὐθαίρετος ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
8:17.targetText: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.

groups.note: Greek μέν ... δέ contrasts acceptance of the appeal with the further eager voluntary action. BSB expresses this discourse pair as not only ... but; the whole contrast construction supplies these markers without inventing an independent Greek not negator.

Greek being more eager he went out is recast as he is eagerly coming. The eager adjective, being participle and movement verb jointly express this predicate; BSB changes departure/past viewpoint to present coming and does not separately express the comparative degree.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek appeal article has no separate English word with our appeal.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB supplies our with the definite appeal; no first-person possessive pronoun is written in this N1904 phrase.
